chapter: Recording dates, Goodman and band life
title: What Benny Goodman was like: the stare and his comment about Nancy Wilson
summary: Jones barely knew Goodman, mentions the famous ray and Jess Stacy's opinion, and Goodman praising his writing for Nancy Wilson.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: What was Benny Goodman like to work for?
Let me see. It's kind of hard to describe him, because I wasn't around him that much, you know?
Uh-huh.
He had a steady -- I think we called it a ray, a stare. He'd look at you.
What did it mean?
You never knew. You know. I think it was
just a gimmick he had going. (Laughter) Oh, everybody used to speak about it, you know, I'd heard of it. He had -- the ray had more reputation than he did.
(Laughter)
In fact, Jess Stacy, who lives right up here on Lookout Mountain Avenue --
Oh, he does? I didn't know that.

Yeah. We used to have block association meetings, you know, so we were both talking about Benny. So Jess would say, "That son of a gun is crazy." You know, he'd say, "There's nothing wrong with him, he's just crazy."
I've heard a lot of opinions. I don't know.
Yeah. So I said, "Well, I wasn't sure." I didn't stay there that long.
Uh-huh.
And then another time I remember him speaking quite well about my writing with Nancy. Where did I see him? He says, "That girl, Nancy Wilson, you know?"
Uh-huh.
That's when she was breaking through, really.
Uh-huh.
And after she'd done the thing with
Cannonball, you know, the jazz thing.
Uh-huh.
And then I came out here to write with her, and the chemistry turned out right then, you know?
Yeah, you did some nice things with Nancy.
And he says, "Oh, that girl Nancy Wilson," he says, "I like that stuff you wrote." I was hoping he would say, "Would you write me some?"
(Laughter)
But he didn't take the conversation any further than the compliment.
